jobDescription: Harbour Mutual is a regional retail bank with about 400,000 active mobile-app users. The Product Manager for mobile payments owns the roadmap for transfers, payees and payment requests, runs customer discovery, writes requirements with the engineering squads and agrees payment controls with compliance and fraud colleagues. The role is accountable for taking features from pilot to production launch, including the release decision with the change board and monitoring after launch, and it reports monthly to the digital steering group. The product team works in three squads and follows the bank's change-management policy for every app release.
requirements: Runs customer discovery and turns findings into prioritised requirements.
Works with compliance and fraud teams to agree payment controls before release.
Has taken a customer-facing banking feature from pilot to production launch, including the release decision and post-launch monitoring.
Maintains a prioritised roadmap and backlog with engineering squads.
Reports product progress to senior stakeholders.

evidence.text: Associate Product Manager, Calder Building Society, February 2022 to October 2024: ran 18 discovery interviews with members who split bills or collect money for clubs, then wrote the problem statement and requirements for in-app payment requests, putting the three needs raised most often first.

Agreed payment-request limits and confirmation-of-payee checks with the compliance and fraud teams and recorded each control in the feature's risk assessment, which the second-line risk team reviewed before the pilot started.
Ran a six-week colleague pilot of payment requests in the internal beta build of the app with 150 staff accounts, gathering feedback through an in-app survey.
Kept the payments squad's backlog in priority order and co-wrote the quarterly roadmap with the engineering lead, re-ranking items after each sprint review.
Presented a monthly payments update to the digital steering group covering backlog progress, pilot feedback and open risks, with a one-page summary sent the day before.

Work sample: the close-out deck for the colleague pilot, with survey results, defect counts and the open-risk list. Every slide footer reads 'Internal beta build - staff accounts only'. The slide headed 'Launch' states 'Launched 9 November - payment requests live in the app', above a screenshot captured from the beta build.
Reference check summary: Calder's head of digital confirmed in writing that the candidate ran the six-week colleague pilot and presented the monthly payments updates to the steering group.
HR verification note: the title Associate Product Manager and the dates February 2022 to October 2024 were checked against Calder Building Society's written employment reference.

propositions.text: The candidate launched payment requests to the society's customers in production on 9 November and monitored the feature after launch.
propositions.rationale: The launch wording sits in a pilot close-out deck whose every footer limits it to the internal beta build and staff accounts, and the screenshot comes from the beta build; no source says the feature reached customers in production. The deployment rule forbids describing a pilot as a production launch.

propositions.text: The candidate ran a six-week colleague pilot of payment requests in the internal beta build with 150 staff accounts.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the pilot and its scope, and the reference check confirms it in writing.

propositions.text: The candidate agreed payment-request limits and confirmation-of-payee checks with the compliance and fraud teams.
propositions.rationale: The resume states the controls and that they were recorded in the risk assessment.

gold.expectedGap: Only the colleague pilot in the internal beta build is documented; a customer-facing production launch, the release decision and post-launch monitoring are not.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the pilot as a six-week colleague pilot in the internal beta build with staff accounts; do not turn the deck's 'Launch' slide into a customer launch.
followUpTargets: Ask whether payment requests were released to customers after the pilot, who made the release decision, and what the candidate monitored after any launch.
